group.passage: Like many high schools in Taiwan, Linden High gives its students a half-hour nap after lunch, with the lights turned off and heads resting on desks. This month, the school newspaper asked readers whether the nap should continue, and some of their replies are shown below.

passage_parts.label: A
passage_parts.title: Kevin
passage_parts.text: I have never been able to fall asleep with my head on a hard wooden desk. Every day I just lie there with a sore neck and listen to everyone else breathing. I would much rather spend that time finishing my math homework.

passage_parts.label: B
passage_parts.title: Ruby
passage_parts.text: Everyone is arguing about the nap, but nobody mentions the real problem: we get so much homework that most of us go to bed far too late. A short nap after lunch can’t make up for a short night of sleep.

passage_parts.label: C
passage_parts.title: Wendy
passage_parts.text: I used to think the nap was something for little kids, but I have changed my mind. After twenty minutes of rest, I can concentrate in chemistry class instead of watching the clock. Please don’t take it away from us!

passage_parts.label: D
passage_parts.title: Jason
passage_parts.text: Unless you go to bed after midnight every night, there is no reason to sleep at school. Students like me who already get enough rest at home are simply wasting half an hour. I say we drop the nap and finish classes earlier.

passage_parts.label: E
passage_parts.title: Ms. Chen
passage_parts.text: Before the school added the nap, my first class after lunch was a sea of yawns and empty faces. These days, hands go up again when I ask a question. I won’t pretend to know the science, but I trust what I see in front of me.

passage_parts.label: F
passage_parts.title: Mrs. Kao
passage_parts.text: My son comes home every day with a red mark on his face from sleeping on his desk. In my opinion, sleep belongs in a bed, not at school. Teachers should give less homework so that students can rest properly at home.

passage_parts.label: G
passage_parts.title: Tony
passage_parts.text: As class leader, I have to make sure everyone is quiet during the nap, so I never get a moment to rest myself. To be honest, those thirty minutes are the hardest part of my whole school day.

passage_parts.label: H
passage_parts.title: Nurse Wang
passage_parts.text: A short rest after lunch really does help most teenagers, and I am glad our school offers one. Students are less likely to doze off in class later in the day. It should be short, though, because a longer nap can leave you feeling heavy and slow all afternoon.

questions.stem:
From (A) to (H) in the replies above, which ONES are in favor of the nap?
請選出留言者前的英文大寫字母，並劃記在答題卷作答區內。（多選題，4分）
Which phrase in the replies means “to balance out a loss or a lack of something”?（簡答題，2分）

1.explanation_zh: 支持午休的 Wendy 說，休息二十分鐘後，她在化學課上能專心（concentrate），不再一直盯著時鐘。摘要句 improves students’ ___ 的所有格後面要名詞，把動詞 concentrate 轉成名詞 concentration（專注力）。
evidence: After twenty minutes of rest, I can concentrate in chemistry class instead of watching the clock.
1.strategy_zh: 摘要句說的是「支持者」的理由，先找出支持午休的留言，再找午休帶來的好處；所有格（students’）後面要名詞，動詞要轉成名詞。
hints: 找支持午休的學生留言，看午休讓她在下午的課上能做到什麼。
文中的動詞是 concentrate，請改成名詞。

2.explanation_zh: Kevin 說他趴在硬木桌上根本睡不著，每天只是躺在那裡（lie there）、脖子痠痛。spend + 時間 + V-ing 是「花時間做某事」的句型，lie 的 V-ing 形是 lying（ie 改成 y 再加 -ing），lying awake＝醒著躺著；後面的 unable to rest at all 也呼應他根本沒辦法休息。
evidence: Every day I just lie there with a sore neck and listen to everyone else breathing.
2.strategy_zh: 看到 spend the whole break 就知道後面要接 V-ing；再找反對者描述自己午休時「睡不著、只能怎樣」的句子。注意 lie 的 -ing 形拼法。
hints: spend + 時間 + ___：動詞要用 V-ing。
找說自己在桌上睡不著的學生，看他午休時都在做什麼。
文中是 lie there，請寫出 lie 的 V-ing 形（注意拼法）。

3.explanation_zh: (C) Wendy 說午休讓她能專心，請學校不要取消，明確支持。(H) 王護理師說午休確實有幫助、很高興學校提供，明確支持。(E) 陳老師沒有直接說「保留」，但她描述加了午休後，下午第一節課從一片呵欠變成有人舉手，而且說她相信親眼看到的，態度是支持（要推論）。(D) Jason 的 unless 條件句講的是「熬夜到半夜的人」，他自己認為午休是浪費時間、主張取消，不是支持。(A) 睡不著、寧可寫作業；(B) 認為午休補不回睡眠不足，真正的問題是作業太多；(F) 認為睡覺應該在家；(G) 說午休是一天中最辛苦的時段，都不是支持保留。
evidence: Please don’t take it away from us!
A short rest after lunch really does help most teenagers, and I am glad our school offers one.
These days, hands go up again when I ask a question.
I won’t pretend to know the science, but I trust what I see in front of me.
Unless you go to bed after midnight every night, there is no reason to sleep at school.
I say we drop the nap and finish classes earlier.

option_notes_zh.A: Kevin 趴在桌上睡不著，寧可拿這段時間寫數學作業，不支持午休。
option_notes_zh.B: Ruby 認為午休補不回晚上睡眠不足，真正該解決的是作業太多，沒有表示支持保留午休。
option_notes_zh.D: unless 條件句講的是「每天過半夜才睡的人」，Jason 自己認為午休是浪費半小時，主張取消、提早放學。條件句容易讓人誤以為他有條件地支持。
option_notes_zh.F: 高媽媽認為睡覺應該在床上、不是在學校，主張少出作業讓學生回家好好休息，不支持午休。
option_notes_zh.G: Tony 身為班長要維持秩序，自己完全不能休息，說這是一天中最辛苦的時段，沒有表示支持。

3.strategy_zh: 態度分類題：逐則判斷「贊成／反對／沒表態」，並找出表態的那一句。注意 unless、if 這類條件句是在講誰，以及說話者最後的結論；沒有直接說「保留」的留言，要從描述的效果推論態度。
hints: 逐則留言判斷：對保留午休是贊成、反對，還是沒有表態？
有一則留言沒有直接說贊成，但描述了加入午休後課堂的改變。
Jason 的 unless 條件句是在說誰？他最後主張什麼？

A: I would much rather spend that time finishing my math homework.
B: A short nap after lunch can’t make up for a short night of sleep.
C: After twenty minutes of rest, I can concentrate in chemistry class instead of watching the clock.
Please don’t take it away from us!
D: Unless you go to bed after midnight every night, there is no reason to sleep at school.
I say we drop the nap and finish classes earlier.
E: Before the school added the nap, my first class after lunch was a sea of yawns and empty faces.
These days, hands go up again when I ask a question.
I won’t pretend to know the science, but I trust what I see in front of me.
F: In my opinion, sleep belongs in a bed, not at school.
G: To be honest, those thirty minutes are the hardest part of my whole school day.
H: A short rest after lunch really does help most teenagers, and I am glad our school offers one.

4.explanation_zh: make up for 是「彌補、抵銷（損失或不足）」。Ruby 說午餐後的短暫午睡，彌補不了晚上睡太少。
evidence: A short nap after lunch can’t make up for a short night of sleep.
4.strategy_zh: 定義題：先把英文定義換成中文「彌補不足」，再找哪一則留言在談「睡眠不夠能不能補回來」；答案只寫三個字的片語，不要把 can’t 一起抄。
hints: 定義以 to 開頭，要找動詞片語。
找一則認為「午休補不回晚上睡太少」的留言。
答案是三個字，第一個字是 make。

translation_zh.text:
和臺灣許多高中一樣，林登高中讓學生在午餐後午睡半小時，燈關掉，大家趴在桌上休息。這個月，校刊問讀者午休該不該繼續，以下是部分回覆。

A（Kevin）我趴在硬邦邦的木頭桌上從來睡不著。每天我只是趴在那裡，脖子痠痛，聽著其他人的呼吸聲。我寧可把這段時間拿來寫完數學作業。

B（Ruby）大家都在爭論午休，卻沒有人提到真正的問題：我們作業多到大部分人都太晚才睡。午餐後短短的午睡，彌補不了晚上睡太少。

C（Wendy）我以前覺得午休是小孩子的事，但我改變想法了。休息二十分鐘後，我上化學課能專心，不會一直盯著時鐘。拜託不要把午休拿走！

D（Jason）除非你每天都過了半夜才睡，否則根本沒理由在學校睡覺。像我這樣在家已經睡夠的學生，只是在浪費半小時。我說乾脆取消午休，早點放學。

E（陳老師）學校還沒加入午休之前，我午餐後的第一節課滿是呵欠和茫然的臉。現在我一問問題，又有人舉手了。我不敢說自己懂背後的科學，但我相信親眼看到的。

F（高媽媽）我兒子每天回家，臉上都有趴在桌上睡出來的紅印。我認為睡覺該在床上，不是在學校。老師應該少出點作業，讓學生能在家好好休息。

G（Tony）身為班長，我午休時得確保大家都很安靜，自己一刻也不能休息。老實說，那三十分鐘是我在學校一整天裡最辛苦的時段。

H（王護理師）午餐後短暫休息對大多數青少年確實有幫助，我很高興我們學校有提供。學生在當天稍後的課堂上比較不會打瞌睡。不過午睡應該短一點，因為睡太久可能讓你整個下午都覺得昏沉遲鈍。

evidence: After twenty minutes of rest, I can concentrate in chemistry class instead of watching the clock.
1.explanation_zh: students’ 後需名詞；支持者 Wendy 說午睡後上課能專心，concentrate 的名詞為 concentration。

evidence: Every day I just lie there with a sore neck and listen to everyone else breathing.
2.explanation_zh: spend time + V-ing，且後接 awake；Kevin 睡不著只是躺著，lie 的現在分詞為 lying。

evidence: Please don’t take it away from us!
These days, hands go up again when I ask a question.
A short rest after lunch really does help most teenagers, and I am glad our school offers one.
3.explanation_zh: Wendy 請學校別取消午睡、Ms. Chen 看到午睡後學生上課有精神、Nurse Wang 很高興學校提供午休，三人支持；Kevin、Jason、Mrs. Kao、Tony 反對或抱怨，Ruby 只指出作業太多的問題，沒有支持午睡。

C: I used to think the nap was something for little kids, but I have changed my mind.
Please don’t take it away from us!
E: Before the school added the nap, my first class after lunch was a sea of yawns and empty faces.
These days, hands go up again when I ask a question.
H: A short rest after lunch really does help most teenagers, and I am glad our school offers one.

evidence: A short nap after lunch can’t make up for a short night of sleep.
4.explanation_zh: make up for 意為彌補（損失或不足），Ruby 說短暫午睡無法彌補睡眠不足。

evidence: After twenty minutes of rest, I can concentrate in chemistry class instead of watching the clock.
1.explanation_zh: 支持者說午睡讓學生下午上課更專心；improves students' 後要名詞，concentrate 的名詞形是 concentration。

evidence: Every day I just lie there with a sore neck and listen to everyone else breathing.
2.explanation_zh: 批評者說整個午休只是躺著睡不著；spend ... 後接動名詞，lie 變成 lying。

evidence: After twenty minutes of rest, I can concentrate in chemistry class instead of watching the clock.
These days, hands go up again when I ask a question.
A short rest after lunch really does help most teenagers, and I am glad our school offers one.
3.explanation_zh: Wendy、Ms. Chen、Nurse Wang 都肯定午睡的效果；Kevin、Jason、Mrs. Kao 反對，Ruby 和 Tony 沒有表態支持。

C: After twenty minutes of rest, I can concentrate in chemistry class instead of watching the clock.
E: These days, hands go up again when I ask a question.
H: A short rest after lunch really does help most teenagers, and I am glad our school offers one.

evidence: A short nap after lunch can’t make up for a short night of sleep.
4.explanation_zh: make up for 表示彌補損失或不足，文中指午睡彌補不了睡眠不足。

A.evidence: I would much rather spend that time finishing my math homework.
A.explanation_zh: Kevin 在桌上睡不著，寧可拿午休時間寫作業，不支持午休（ST）。

B.evidence: A short nap after lunch can’t make up for a short night of sleep.
B.explanation_zh: Ruby 認為午休補不回晚上睡眠不足，真正的問題是作業太多；她沒有表示支持保留午休（ST）。

D.evidence: I say we drop the nap and finish classes earlier.
D.explanation_zh: unless 條件句講的是每天過半夜才睡的人；Jason 自己主張取消午休、提早放學，是反對（ST*）。

F.evidence: In my opinion, sleep belongs in a bed, not at school.
F.explanation_zh: 高媽媽認為睡覺應該在家裡的床上，不是在學校，不支持午休（ST）。

G.evidence: To be honest, those thirty minutes are the hardest part of my whole school day.
G.explanation_zh: Tony 身為班長要維持秩序、自己不能休息，說午休是一天最辛苦的時段，沒有支持午休（ST）。
